grades.quote: Any file descriptors descended from that same call to `open` share the same open file description. For example, in the previous example of `ls` and `ps` writing to the `information` file, each of the two processes has its own file descriptor, but they are referring to the same open file description, and hence share the same file offset.
grades.reason: Explains that descendant file descriptors share one open file description and thus one file offset, and that lseek changes that offset. It also notes that a separate open() gets a separate offset. It never names fork explicitly, so the fork-to-seek link has to be inferred.

grades.quote: Two file descriptors share an offset if they were derived from the same original file descriptor by a sequence of fork and dup calls. Otherwise file descriptors do not share offsets, even if they resulted from open calls for the same file.
grades.reason: States that file descriptors derived through fork (and dup) share an offset, while separate opens do not. So an offset change through one descriptor, such as a seek, is visible through the other. It does not mention seek explicitly.
